cohorts.label: 2-20h
cohorts.summary: Reviewers highlight strict time limits, terrain collision bugs during frantic escapes, multiplayer stuttering, and single-player restrictions on expansions.

claims.claim: Reviewers note that the campaign features strict time limits and tasks involving timed escapes or collecting items under tight deadlines.

citations.review_text:
Teardown features quite literally the best destruction system in video gaming history, built entirely on fully interactive voxels where literally every single tiny piece can be dynamically smashed, blown up, and torn apart.

Teardown's campaign however is a massive failure on its gameplay side, with almost every single mission turning into a frustrating, stressful, and unfun mess of strict time limits and undefeatable enemies that completely contradicts the sandbox destruction idea.

However, this review remains overwhelmingly positive because the voxel destruction system is the absolute best in any video game to date, and the sandbox mode and mod support are awesome, unique, and exceptionally well done.

My advice: "ACTUALLY Disable Alarm completely [MP]", easily found in the Workshop, is basically required to play the campaign. Also, the "Hook Shotgun" helps in the helicopter and robot levels.
I honestly find this game quite fun but the campaign becomes extremely boring when all of the missions are grab 5 items in under 60s and get out

claims.claim: Reviewers report getting stuck in the terrain due to the voxel implementation, which causes frustration during timed challenges.

citations.review_text:
Teardown features quite literally the best destruction system in video gaming history, built entirely on fully interactive voxels where literally every single tiny piece can be dynamically smashed, blown up, and torn apart.

Teardown's campaign however is a massive failure on its gameplay side, with almost every single mission turning into a frustrating, stressful, and unfun mess of strict time limits and undefeatable enemies that completely contradicts the sandbox destruction idea.

However, this review remains overwhelmingly positive because the voxel destruction system is the absolute best in any video game to date, and the sandbox mode and mod support are awesome, unique, and exceptionally well done.

My advice: "ACTUALLY Disable Alarm completely [MP]", easily found in the Workshop, is basically required to play the campaign. Also, the "Hook Shotgun" helps in the helicopter and robot levels.

Getting stuck in terrain constantly is a non-starter in a game that puts you on a 60 second clock. It's 100% the problem with the voxel implementation, and had they fixed it, it will have been a decent game. Otherwise it's just an excercise in frustration. I'm not getting my hopes up for the developers addressing is, because Teardown has been out for a while now. Also, as a technical person I imagine a lot of the game code would need to be rewritten from scratch. Which in this case means the good portion of their proprietary voxel engine. I wanted to get the DLCs just a couple of hours ago, as it stands now (and shall continue to do so) I'll simply finish the campaign, uninstall the game and then never think of it ever again.

If you have a decent amount of mods, expect a long loading time

(no hated levels at all or complaints amazing dlc ) Moving on to the time travelers dlc. wowwie, that introduction to the dlc, such a slap in the face with thinking youre just restarting the game and then bAM !! dlc time fu**boy :D then with having to use all this old timey stuff ,…

citations.review_text: Fun sandbox game. Its really good and fun but, its actually only more fun with mods. Still great though the campaign is pretty good too although I am mostly a sandbox player.
